correctness.rationale: The n antipodal edges enforce at most one selected endpoint per pair. Outer-cycle adjacency reduces all full assignments to a twisted two-sign cycle, consistent iff n odd; deleting one pair when n even leaves a path with exactly two solutions per hole. Every optimal exchange necessarily moves the hole to a neighboring pair; the two moves are rotations by ±(n-1), which generate Z/(2n) because n is even. Distinct finite enumerators and adjacency constructors passed for every n from 3 through 15, including boundaries 3 and 4.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge comparison of primary full texts, scalar tables and published mathematical findings identifies no theorem implying the entire exchange graph. The known independence number and general TJ=TS move-equivalence are not claimed as new; the homotopy type of an independence complex does not determine the exchange graph of its maximum faces. Direct alias and broader-coverage searches were performed. Bibliographic nonexhaustiveness remains a residual risk. A prior graded independent-domination polynomial for the same Möbius ladder family implies the counts 2 and 2n; a prior near-maximum odd-width maximal-independent-set slide-graph theorem concerns a different cardinality. Neither identifies the maximum-layer exchange edges. These prior state counts are explicitly acknowledged and not claimed as original.

value.rationale: The structure of the space of optimal stable sets in a canonical cubic symmetric graph family is an independent invariant that the known scalar independence number and homotopy types do not determine. The exact sharp parity transition from two mutually inaccessible maxima to a single cycle of 2n maxima, together with a transparent movable-frustration-defect mechanism, supplies a useful complete infinite-family classification and explicit reconfiguration paths.
